picks.blurb: Previewing the New York Jets’ opposition: Miami Dolphins - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers' stunning comeback Valkyries even WNBA Finals Kimi Antonelli on US GP pole NFL injury updates Tatum downplays beef Previewing the New York Jets’ opposition: Miami Dolphins EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - DECEMBER 07: Jordyn Brooks #20 of the Miami Dolphins in action during the NFL 2025 game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on December 07, 2025 in East Rutherford, New Jersey."" (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bent Double Sat, October 24, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Miami Dolphins has won six out of the last seven, 10 of the last 12 and 14 of the last 17 against the New York Jets. However, they enter Sunday's clash at MetLife Stadium as a winless underdog. Let's break down the Dolphins' roster going position by position: The Dolphins had a strange approach to the offseason, primarily heading into a rebuild as they traded guys away and looked to shed salary. This is a team that had six pro bowlers in 2023, but now all six are off the team. However, they coupled that approach with the signing of the biggest prize in this year's free agent quarterback market when they signed Malik Willis to a three-year deal. Willis is getting a chance to be a full-time starter for the first time and he's had mixed results due to the lack of a supporting cast around him. So far, he's completed just 56 percent of his passes with two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and four interceptions. The backup to Willis is Kyle McCord, who has never thrown an NFL pass. Offensive Line Despite making so many other changes, Miami retained most of their offensive line and built on the foundation already in place by drafting Kadyn Proctor in the first round and putting him into the starting line-up at left guard. The rest of their starters were all also starting for them last year, although former first round right tackle Austin Jackson only started the first game and the last five due to injuries. The other three starters are center Aaron Brewer, left tackle Patrick Paul and right guard Jonah Savaiinaea. Savaiinaea struggled badly as a second round rookie last season and he was knocked out of the last game due to injury with Jarrett Kingston filling in for him the rest of the way. Miami's starting tackles have given up five sacks and eight penalties between them so far this season. The other backups include Andrew Meyer – who started a game at center last year – and sixth round rookie DJ Campbell. Chukwuebuka Godrick and Caedan Wallace round out this group. Running Backs Miami's plans for the year further shifted towards rebuild mode when they lost their star running back De'Von Achane to a torn ACL early in the season. The starter is now Ollie Gordon II, who – to his credit – is averaging five yards per carry with three rushing touchdowns. Jaylen Wright is the main backup, but Miami also has rookie Kaytron Allen as the number three. Allen was drafted in the sixth round by the Commanders but did not make their roster. Another rookie, the undrafted DJ Herman, is also on the roster as a fullback. Pass catchers With Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle now gone, Miami is hoping that Malik Washington can develop into a true number one receiver. He has 29 touches in the first five games, but less than 300 yards and no touchdowns. Tight end Greg Dulcich is the only other Dolphins player with double digits in catches. In order to find Willis some passing game weapons, Miami went pass catcher heavy in the middle rounds of the draft. Receivers Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas were selected along with tight end Will Kacmarek in the third round and then another receiver, Kevin Coleman, and another tight end, Seydou Traore, were picked in the fifth. Out of all of these, the Jets may view Bell as the biggest threat as they had Malik McClain operating as him during the week on the scout team, presumably in an effort to try and replicate his combination of size and athleticism. Bell had a nice game against the Chiefs with four catches but otherwise only has two other touches all year. Those two touches gained 25 and 26 yards though, so he may be a chunk play threat. Douglas is also a threat. He caught five passes for 94 yards in his NFL debut in the opener, but then got hurt in week two and hasn't played since. He'll make his return on Sunday. Further depth comes from receivers Jalen Tolbert and Jared Wayne, and from tight end Justin Joly. Defensive Line Miami's defense got a boost in the game before the bye week with the return of last year's first round pick Kenneth Grant at defensive tackle. Grant had been dealing with a toe issue but should now see his playing time increase alongside Zach Sieler. Sieler has been a thorn in the side of the Jets for several years with eight sacks in his past six games against them. Miami has won 10 of 12 games over the Jets with Sieler in the line-up. With Grant out, Jordan Phillips and Zeek Biggers had been sharing the workload alongside Sieler, who has a team-high two sacks. Miami's best edge rusher is Chop Robinson, but the former first rounder's production has been inconsistent. He had three sacks in four games towards the end of last year but only has one in five since then. The other starter on the edge is Josh Uche with Malik Herring as the main backup. Robert Beal Jr. and undrafted rookie Rodney McGraw are also on the roster, but Beal has been listed as doubtful with a hamstring issue. At linebacker, Miami is getting excellent production from their second round pick, Jacob Rodriguez, who has 57 tackles and an interception in his first five NFL games. Rodriguez starts alongside last year's leading tackler, Jordyn Brooks, with Willie Gay also getting plenty of reps. Gay is questionable with an illness, but did return to practice on Friday. Shaka Heyward and Jackson Woodard are the other backups with fourth round pick Trey Moore on injured reserve. Defensive Backs Miami's depth is slightly compromised in the secondary, as fourth round safety Kyle Louis and veteran safety Ronnie Harrison are both on injured reserve. In addition, cornerback Darrell Baker remains on the PUP list. Louis did return to practice this week so could be activated for Sunday. He's officially questionable. The starters right now at safety are Dante Trader Jr. and fifth round rookie Michael Taaffe. Trader leads the team with three pass breakups but the rookies Taaffe and Rodriguez have been inconsistent tacklers, combing for 14 missed tackles in the first five games. At cornerback, the top three are JuJu Brents, Jason Marshall Jr. and Chris Johnson. The first round rookie Johnson has been the primary slot corner. Brents leads the team with four defensive penalties. Further depth comes from safeties Zayne Anderson and Julius Wood, and cornerbacks Marcellas Dial and Reese Taylor, although Taylor has been ruled out due to injury. Miami also has former Jet Jaylin Simpson, who can play safety or corner. Special Teams The Dolphins just made a change at placekicker with another ex-Jet, Riley Patterson, having been released earlier this week after missing three kicks in five games. Zane Gonzalez was added to the practice squad to take over from Patterson. The veteran Bradley Pinion is the Dolphins' punter, but his net average is below 40 yards per punt so far this year. In the return game, Washington is dangerous but hasn't done much this year as his focus has shifted more onto the offense. Wright, who is listed as the backup kickoff returner, had a 79-yard return earlier this season. Coleman is listed as the backup punt returner. The Dolphins also recently released wide receiver Ryan Miller, who had been a primary gunner. Simpson and Dial would be options to handle this role on Sunday. So far this year Woodard and Simpson have been productive in coverage.

away.headline: Dolphins' Jeff Hafley returns to New Jersey seeking first Miami win
away.blurb: Coach Jeff Hafley hopes to get his first NFL head-coaching win in his home state of New Jersey. Players have identified key areas for improvement, including reducing turnovers and penalties. MIAMI GARDENS ― Miami Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley likes to say it's about the team and not about him, but he sure would like to have his first NFL head-coaching win take place in his home state of New Jersey. "My mom will be there," Hafley said of a Week 7 game at the New York Jets . "I'll have a lot of people there. My brother, my sister, I'll probably have 30-plus people at the game. For all of us, I think it's always nice to go back close to home." Hafley hails from Montvale, N.J., only 17 miles from MetLife Stadium where Sunday's game will be played. The Dolphins are 0-5 but entered the week only 4.5-point underdogs at the Jets , who are 2-4. Miami's first five opponents were NFL playoff contenders. The Jets likely are not. And here is more good news: the Dolphins are coming off of an early bye week. "New energy, man," said Dolphins linebacker Jordyn Brooks. "Just a chance to reset. Wasn't a friendly first five weeks of the season. It was tough, kind of going through that. And we still got to live with it, but I think that break gives you a chance to kind of reflect and kind of take a deep breath and I think that's what this team needed." Predictably, the Dolphins' statistical resume after five games is poor. Miami ranks better than the league average in only 8 of the top 32 essential categories sorted and ranked by the NFL. What have the Dolphins done fairly well? "Right now, we're a team that's running the ball very well, and we're playing pretty good run defense, too," Hafley said. "We're a physical team. I think we have to build on that identity and continue to grow and develop." Miami Dolphins seek development, but also a win A lot of growth, development and patience will be required. Coaches often say they use the bye week to "self-scout" in an attempt to improve in areas they may have overlooked in the day-to-day grind of a game week. "With such a small sample size, it's not huge, but a really good time to evaluate and catch your breath and sometimes when you get to step back, you can see some things clearly," Hafley said. There are many areas in which the Dolphins must improve to win a game (short-term goal) and finish better than, say, 2-15 or 3-14 this season. But here are some self-scout reflections Dolphins players have spoken about after the bye. Multiple players have been banged up, including standout rookie receiver Caleb Douglas. It seems the added rest has been a good thing for the young pass catcher, as according to head coach Jeff Hafley, Douglas has a chance to suit up against the New York Jets on the road this upcoming Sunday. home.headline: Why Jets return game has taken step back from dynamic 2025 squad
home.blurb: Why Jets return game has taken step back from dynamic 2025 squad - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Why Jets return game has taken step back from dynamic 2025 squad The 2026 Jets are better than the 2025 Jets in many areas. But one part of the game where it feels like the Jets have taken a step back this year is in the return game. The Jets had a dynamic return game last year with Isaiah Williams and Kene Nwangwu. Williams returned two punts for touchdowns, and Nwangwu returned a kickoff for a touchdown. Each of them had a score in the team's win over the Browns last year. This season, the results are not there. Nwangwu has been battling injuries, but even when he's healthy, the return game has not looked the same. The Jets' longest kick return this year is 36 yards, and the longest punt return is 20 yards. "We want to make sure we get back to that as soon as we can because that helps every part of our football team," Glenn said. "Like last year, it was just a year that I thought our guys, we were just on it. We were hitting it from all different angles, and this year has been tough. Number one, guys understand the other team, so they try to do things to try to negate our return situation. Again, I have full confidence that we'll get back to it. The thing is we just have to strain to finish on those blocks and let our runners run." Brewers' stunning comeback New York Jets wide receiver Isaiah Williams (18) and running back Kene Nwangwu (3) warm up before the start of a game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026. Brian Costello Sun, October 25, 2026 at 12:29 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Jets coach Aaron Glenn said they know it's an area for improvement. Isaiah Williams (18) warms up before the start of the Jets' Week 6 loss to the Patriots in Foxborough, Mass. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Williams said teams have approached them differently this year and are clearly focused on preventing Williams and Nwangwu from having big returns. Still, Williams believes they are going to break one soon. "I think we're very close," Williams said. "I think the biggest thing for us is to continue to do what we do every week. We need to keep practicing, keep putting in the time, focusing on the little details. We know that we have the ability. We know we have the guys. It's just about executing it on Sundays." The Jets placed LB Kiko Mauigoa on injured reserve Saturday. They signed LB Jaden Keller to the active roster and elevated OT Brant Banks and LB Troy Reeder from the practice squad for Sunday's game with the Dolphins.

away.headline: How Buccaneers' Baker Mayfield got help from Tampa Bay Rays on return from thumb injury
away.blurb: How Buccaneers' Baker Mayfield got help from Tampa Bay Rays on return from thumb injury | Sporting News Skip to main content SN 140 Baker Mayfield is set to come back, which is a huge boost for the Buccaneers. But his return from a thumb injury isn't so simple. With his thumb injury being on his throwing hand, playing quarterback might be a bit tricky. But he recently got some help. Rays helped Baker Mayfield with custom glove amid return from thumb injury While the Rays are focused on winning the World Series, Bond was able to help out the city's NFL team by designing a new glove to help Mayfield play through a thumb injury. Horse Racing Horse Racing Latest News More Sports More Sports Latest News Fantasy Fantasy See More Football News Betting Betting See More Explore Betting Home Predictions Prediction Markets See More Explore Predictions Home Watch Watch How to Watch Streaming Services Apple TV Joseph Maiorana/Imagn Images via Reuters Connect The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are currently 1-5 in the regular season and are set to face off against the Carolina Panthers in Week 7. It's a huge game to determine if they'll have a chance of making a playoff run this season. According to Rick Stroud of The Tampa Bay Times , the Tampa Bay Rays actually helped design a new custom glove for Mayfield's right hand leading up to Week 7 to try to help him play without any complications. "Baker Mayfield will wear a glove on his right hand with a solid plate on the back to keep his once-dislocated thumb from bending the wrong way when he likely starts Sunday's game at Carolina," Stroud writes. Helping to make such a glove for Mayfield were the hometown Rays, just about set to face off against the Milwaukee Brewers in MLB's World Series, as the Rays aim for their first-ever championship. But how did the Rays help make this glove for Mayfield to suit up in Week 7 against the Panthers in a must-win matchup? Well, Stroud revealed the one man whose "invention" will help Mayfield take the field without worry this weekend. MORE : Aaron Rodgers blasts Buccaneers' field as 'one of the worst surfaces in the league' "The glove was the invention of Rays home clubhouse attendant Nick Bond, who took a receiver's glove and ripped off the thumb while inserting a support," Stroud writes. "They made two versions: one with hard plastic and another as a soft cast." Assuming Mayfield suits up in Week 7, as is the expectation heading into Friday, he'll be utilizing a custom glove that the Rays helped to create. While the Buccaneers' vibes might be off, this act by the Rays is a very cool moment of city camaraderie. away.headline: Buccaneers Week 7 injury report: Mayfield returns, Egbuka sidelined
away.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers received encouraging news Wednesday as Baker Mayfield returned to full participation in practice after missing three games with a right thumb injury. However, wide receiver Emeka Egbuka was among five players who did not practice as Tampa Bay prepares for Sunday's NFC South matchup against the Carolina Panthers . Luke Goedeke (calf), Bucky Irving (illness), Zyon McCollum (illness) and Christian Rozeboom (finger) also missed practice. Antoine Winfield Jr. was limited with a rib injury, while Sean Tucker and Cody Mauch participated fully. Carolina quarterback Bryce Young fully participated despite a knee injury, while running back Chuba Hubbard was held out for rest. Practice designations: FP = Full Participation; LP = Limited Participation; DNP = Did Not Participate. away.headline: Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers Gameday: Injury Updates, Depth Charts, TV Info, Betting Lines, More
away.blurb: Three Pittsburgh Steelers have been ruled out for the team's Week 6 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, and five more are questionable to suit up, according to the team's Friday injury report. Two wide receivers Ben Skowronek and Roman Wilson left the team's 34-22 Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts with injures and did not return — and they won't be back this week, either. Skowronek suffered a calf injury early in the second quarter, and then Wilson injured his left hand on the final offensive drive of the first half. Wilson had a large wrap on his left hand after the game. On Monday, head coach Mike McCarthy said neither player will return to active this week. Fellow wide receiver DK Metcalf was initially listed as questionable to play after missing practice on Friday with an illness, but he has now been cleared to play. Tight end Pat Freiermuth is also questionable to play after suffering a calf injury in practice on Saturday. Strong safety DeShon Elliott remains limited in practice and will not return this week. Starting cornerback Jamel Dean was ruled out last week, but might be ahead of the curve on the initial multi-week estimate for his injury. He is listed as questionable. Running back Rico Dowdle , who is recovering from a dislocated toe on his left foot, is also questionable to make his return to the lineup, as is defensive tackle Keeanu Benton , who has an ankle injury, and defensive who has an ankle injury, and defensive back Jalen Ramsey , who has played through his broken wrist the last two weeks. A beat up Steelers defensive kept Tom Brady out of the end zone for 55 minutes and Mitch Trubisky successfully replaced an injury Kenny Pickett as Pittsburgh beat the Buccaneers, 20-18 at Acrisure Stadium on Oct. 16, 2022. Pickett threw his first career touchdown pass to Najee Harris in the first quarter, but a hit from blitzing linebacker Devin White knocked him out of the game. Chris Boswell kicked two field goals and Trubisky found Chase Claypool for a six-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter to extend the Steelers lead. With 4:45 to play, Brady finally punched through a defense that was playing without T.J. Watt , Minkah Fitzpatrick , Ahkello Witherspoon , Levi Wallace and Cam Sutton with a touchdown pass to Leonard Fournette, but Devin Bush broke up the two-point conversion attempt, and Trubisky and the Pittsburgh offense ran out the clock. Defensive run game coordinator and outside linebackers coach Larry Foote had two stints with the Steelers, playing from 2002-08 and 2010-13 after the team made him a fifth-round draft pick out of Michigan. Foote was a two-time Super Bowl champion in Pittsburgh and also won a Super Bowl LV ring as a coach with Tampa in 2021. home.headline: Jaelan Phillips is out, but his injury isn’t the only puzzle Panthers have to solve
home.blurb: Canales soon clarified that Phillips will be out for Sunday’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers: “I know there are advantages to game plans, but this is something that we need to address and take care of.” With Phillips officially out — it’s unclear if he’ll be ready by the Panthers’ Thursday Night Football game against the Packers in Week 8 — the Panthers are missing more than a run-of-the-mill defensive starter. The 27-year-old who the Panthers signed to a four-year, $120 million contract this free agency has lived up to his billing as a premier pass rusher; he has 2.5 sacks through five games but has also added 18 total pressures in the pass rush — 24th among all edge rushers , according to Pro Football Focus. Phillips has also been stout against the run and a vocal leader his teammates praise. What’s also a result of Phillips being out? The absence of Phillips comes at the same time as reserve outside linebacker and special teams ace Thomas Incoom is also “week to week” with a calf injury. Incoom exited the Eagles in the first half and didn’t return, and as a result the Panthers needed to do a whole bunch of roster magic to fill his role on special teams. In each of the four special teams units Incoom contributes on — kick return, kick coverage, punt return, punt coverage — the Panthers needed to replace him with four different players, Canales said. Canales was asked if the Panthers will elevate anyone from the practice squad with Phillips and Incoom out, and he indicated that Nick Hampton would. The interior offensive lineman was placed on the team’s injured reserve before the season began due to a hamstring injury and is now waiting for his 21-day practice window to be activated. When asked Wednesday, Canales was vague about Christensen’s situation: “We’re just evaluating it, and you gotta figure out roster spots as well,” before adding that he has faith in the team’s current slate of IOLs. If Christensen were to return, that limits their flexibility to use the injured reserve. It’s also worth noting the Panthers have already waived someone off the injured reserve with an injury settlement — Claudin Cherelus a few weeks ago — to avoid further limitations. It’s possible, perhaps likely, that once Cherelus gets healthy, he’d re-sign with the Panthers, rejoining the squad without forcing the team to use one of its eight precious IR-elevation moves. home.headline: Bucs elevate LB from practice squad for Week 7 vs. Panthers
home.blurb: Fordham will fill in for Rozeboom as the team’s fourth linebacker. Where he will most likely have the biggest impact is on special teams. Rozeboom has been a part of the Bucs core special teams unit, logging 27 snaps on punt coverage, 25 on kick return, 23 on punt return, seven on kick coverage and two on the field goal block unit. In total, Rozeboom’s 84 total special teams snaps rank 10th on the team. His three special teams tackles are tied for sixth-most on the team with tight ends Bauer Sharp and Ko Kieft and fellow linebacker SirVocea Dennis. Fordham is a rookie undrafted free agent out of North Carolina State. The team signed him May 9th, 2026, two weeks after the 2026 NFL Draft. Over five seasons with the Wolfpack he tallied 252 combined tackles, 18.0 for a loss, 4.5 sacks, 1 forced fumble, 2 fumbles recovered, six passes defensed and two interceptions. His 2025 campaign was his best by far as he had 143 tackles, 10 for a loss, 3.5 sacks and both of his career interceptions. The calculus surrounding the team’s roster decisions as it pertains to the 48 players who get a gameday hat change from the past few weeks. With quarterback Baker Mayfield officially questionable on the team’s injury report and all but guaranteed to play, Tampa Bay didn’t need to elevate practice squad quarterback Easton Stick. That helps them avoid a roster crunch issue as Stick was out of elevations and they would have had to add him to the roster or opt to elevate fellow practice squad passer Brett Rypien. But two new starters on the offensive side of the ball join safety Antoine Winfield Jr. as ruled out for the game on Sunday. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, Tampa Bays leader in targets, receptions and receiving yards will miss the game with a concussion and foot injury. The team activated receiver David Sills III off of injured reserve as the corresponding move when they placed Rozeboom on injured reserve. Right tackle Luke Goedeke has a calf injury that will keep him out of the game. Ahead of their Week 7 matchup against their divisional rival Carolina Panthers, the 1-5 Bucs are elevating just one player from their practice squad to their gameday roster, the team announced Saturday. After placing backup linebacker Christian Rozeboom on injured reserve earlier this week due to a finger injury. It makes sense that their practice squad elevation this week would lean towards that position. The team could have elevated two players but opted for only one in Week 7. This isn’t Fordham’s first elevation this year. He was previously elevated and played in Week 4, where he played four snaps on special teams himself without earning a single production stat. He played extensively during the preseason this year, logging four tackles on special teams over three games and 29 snaps. He also tallied 10 tackles and five defensive stops over 12 attempts while adding a pressure over 100 defensive snaps. As for the Baltimore Ravens , their kicker is on notice. These teams meet in a Week 7 AFC North clash, and here are bold predictions for the contest. The Bengals (3-2) enter the game in last place in the division despite having a winning record. That's because the Ravens, Steelers, and surprising Browns all have a record of 4-2. It should be another battle for the Ravens and Bengals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Joe Burrow will riddle the Ravens' defense for 3 TD passes When the Bengals are right, they are tough on offense. And they've been cooking this year, ranking No. 9 in the NFL in points per game. Burrow is connecting on 71.4% of his passes. He has 11 touchdown passes and three interceptions. Look for him to keep the momentum going this week. But Burrow needs to take care of the football, which Zac Taylor said would go a long way in helping the Bengals win, according to Cleveland.com. "The turnovers is what screams at you," Taylor said. "That leads into field position." And Taylor said Burrow and his teammates are ready for this matchup. "It's exciting," Taylor said. "I think our guys really get fired up for this game. Not that they don't get fired up for every game, but whenever we play in Baltimore in a road divisional game, it's a fun one to get up for, and our guys will be up for it." Bengals RB Chase Brown will score two TDs One of them will be on the receiving end of a pass from Burrow. Brown will have a nice day, despite being caught in a time share with Samaje Perine, according to The Athletic. "I think we'll continually assess how that touch share between (Perine) and Chase Brown should play out," Bengals offensive coordinator Pitcher told Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com. "Every game's different. What type of scheme we lean into is going to factor into that. Obviously, what we ran more of yesterday leans into what Samaje does well, which is get downhill and run through contact." The Bengals haven't forgotten about their ground game. "You strive for balance when it comes to run-pass," Pitcher said. "You're always wanting to be the most balanced and versatile version of yourselves. It's like those are high-level goals that you set out to attain. But never in any given situation are we going to let a high-level theoretical goal get in the way of what it means on Sunday to win a game and what is the feedback we're getting in a game on a given Sunday." Derrick Henry will rush for 80-plus yards and a TD Henry is still smarting from last week's fumble that led to the Ravens' loss to the Browns. He took blame for the game-changing turnover , according to ESPN. "I got to take care of the ball," he said. "There's no excuses for that. I got to be better. I put the team in harm's way. I sound like a broken record with this, but I got to go back to work on it. Can't put the team in that situation." Teammate Kyle Hamilton took up for Henry. "Obviously, he's Derrick Henry, Hall of Fame running back [who] wants to hold onto the ball," Hamilton said. "He knows that. He's his harshest critic, so I'm not going to say anything ill about it. He's put us in position to win a lot of games." All of this will motivate Henry for a big game against the Bengals Ravens WR Ja'Kobi Lane will catch 5 passes and score a TD Lane looked ready to roll against the Browns in his return from injury. And he should be able to carve out a significant role in Week 7. Lane looked great in training camp. The injury short-circuited his 2026 season. But now he's back in the mix. His overall stat line could be impacted if Tyler Huntley is still at quarterback. But if Jackson is back, this could be a breakout game for Lane. Who will win the game? The Bengals should be able to outscore the Ravens in this matchup. But the key factor is Jackson. If he's back, the Ravens have a much better chance of winning. But we will still roll with Burrow, Chase, and Tee Higgins having a big game, along with Brown doing his thing. Our AFC North beat writers certainly see a barnburner when looking at their predictions. Expectations were high for both of these divisional foes, but bumps in the road have been faced on both sidelines of this rivalry. Cincinnati is trying to prove its legitimacy as a Super Bowl contender and defeat a winning team. The Ravens are dealing with familiar problems under a new coaching staff, but formidable talent is still spread across the roster. Such is the case for both rosters, really. CBS' lead broadcast crew is calling this game for a reason . It should be a close contest akin to the majority of meetings these teams have had this decade. Our AFC North beat writers certainly see a barnburner when looking at their predictions. Bengals 30, Ravens 27 The big question entering the week was whether or not the Ravens will have quarterback Lamar Jackson for this AFC North battle. After practicing each of the last two days , it's looking like he'll play. Dropping to 4-3 on the season and 0-2 in divisional play would be a rough start for Baltimore, and this game against the Bengals is one they badly need. Baltimore struggled badly on offense against the Browns after the first few drives of the game, and Week 7 will be another tough test against a good Bengals' defensive front. Cincinnati is well rested off an early bye week, and the road team in this matchup is in a similar situation: trying not to start 0-2 in AFC North play. The thing is, I believe the Bengals have an easier home to climb out of if they drop this game. With that being said, I have to roll with the Bengals coming out of the bye week. Baltimore looks like a lesser product on the field aside from Jackson at quarterback, and Burrow will have success finding his weapons against their defense. These games are always close; this one will be too. – Brandon Little, A to Z Cleveland Baltimore Ravens vs. Cincinnati Bengals History This is the 61st regular season meeting between the two franchises, and 62nd overall. Baltimore leads the all-time series, 33-28. Cincinnati won the lone playoff meeting, 24-17, during the 2022-23 NFL postseason. Lamar Jackson is 6-2 against Joe Burrow when both quarterbacks started and played the entire game. Ravens 26, Bengals 24 This is a game Bengals fans should be genuinely excited to watch. If championship aspirations are to be taken seriously, a road game against the biggest adversary in the division is an environment in which the moment is met. That doesn't mean victory is certain. The margin for error against knowledgable rival players is extremely small, but that's not an excuse to not at least look the part. Cincinnati should play well in this game. If the opposite becomes true, then it will say a lot more about where things actually stand with both the roster and coaching staff. Ultimately, I think the Ravens have a better chance of winning when it comes to the details. Derrick Henry hasn't always been efficient this year, but he's built to attack the current weaknesses of the Bengals defense. Jackson's track record against multiple iterations of the unit is solid. Baltimore may have a systemic issue blowing leads, but is Cincinnati's offense ready to finish games against a quality team? Something may give there. That's a long way to say this should be as close as it gets. Because it's likely Jackson out there and not Tyler Huntley, I'll predict the home team comes out on top. – John Sheeran, A to Z Cincinnati Assuming Jackson is back for the Ravens, this game becomes one of the best on the Sunday slate. The Bengals were off last week, while the Ravens fell to the Browns in a tight game in Cleveland. One would assume that if Jackson is playing in that game, the Ravens escape the Dawg Pound with a win. But now they face the potential of dropping two straight. The problem for Baltimore isn't just that they are playing a good Bengals team; they are playing a team off a bye, where they will be rested and prepared. We have seen some crazy battles between Burrow and Jackson over the years, and I believe we could be in for another shootout, but the Bengals offense will prove to be overwhelming for a Ravens defense that has largely been inconsistent on the back end. Give me Cincy. – Rob Gregson, A to Z Pittsburgh Final Prediction for Bengals at Steelers Two out of three predictions go the Bengals' way. Last year's series ended in a 1-1 split for the first time since the 2022 season. No one would be surprised if this year ends the same. It starts with one team landing the first blow. Unless it's a tie, in which case literally no one wins. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. away.headline: Ravens’ Lamar Jackson practices again, raising hopes for return vs. Bengals
away.blurb: Both Jackson and backup quarterback Tyler Huntley met with the media on Friday afternoon at the Ravens’ Owings Mills practice facility. By rule, teams must make their starting quarterback available to reporters at least once during the week leading up to a game. Having both quarterbacks available, though, was highly unusual. Typically, Jackson meets with reporters every Wednesday during the season. But with his status in question because of an injury, Baltimore waited until Friday each of the past two weeks to rule him out and make Huntley available. Jackson was officially listed as questionable Friday, leaving open the possibility that he could return for Sunday’s pivotal AFC North showdown against the Cincinnati Bengals. He took the podium in shorts and a T-shirt, his left ankle still heavily taped, offering little certainty about what the next two days might bring. Jackson practiced for a third consecutive day Friday, again on a limited basis. On its own, that was encouraging. But practice participation and playing a full game are two different things, and Jackson made it clear that foot pain remains a significant obstacle. The Ravens are also clearly trying to give the Bengals something to think about. There’s also his $260 million contract, which runs through the 2027 season but carries a salary-cap hit of more than $84 million next year. The sides couldn’t hammer out a deal this offseason , so they must address it soon. “If I can just go out there and feel the pain a little bit, I can play,” he said. “But [if] I’m restricted and I can’t do what I do, I’m not helping nobody. If I can just go out there and just be a statue and be hit, that’s not helping my team at all. That’s just me. I feel like I’m being selfish, because it’s about me at that point, for me to go out there and be hurt.” Ravens sack leader Tavius Robinson ruled out for season with injury Ravens outside linebacker Tavius Robinson was ruled out for Sunday after suffering a season-ending pectoral injury . Safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) is also out for this week. Defensive tackle Broderick Washington (tackle) is questionable, while cornerback T.J. Tampa (knee) is doubtful as he continues his return from injured reserve. Will Lamar Jackson play? Or won’t he? “I’m heading in the right direction,” Jackson said in his first comments to reporters since suffering the injury midway through an Oct. 4 win over the Tennessee Titans. “I can’t call it right now. “I feel like the swelling went down a lot, but just the pain tolerance. I’m just trying to move how I move. If I can’t do that, I can’t help my team. I can’t put my team in a situation like that. I feel like I’m doing a disservice then. … I can walk. It’s just trying to run, and [I can’t] put too much pressure.” “Between Lamar and our staff and us, it’s gonna be a decision based on him and how he feels and how effective he can be,” coach Jesse Minter said. “He’s had a good couple days, but we’ll see how it goes over the next 48 hours.

away.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens enter Week 7 against the Cincinnati Bengals with their biggest offensive question still unanswered. Lamar Jackson is questionable with an ankle injury after participating on a limited basis in all three practices, leaving Baltimore to prepare without certainty at quarterback. Jackson’s practice involvement keeps a return possible, but the report offers no confirmation that he will play. His availability remains the central storyline for an offense that must account for both his passing ability and the pressure his mobility puts on opposing defenses. Baltimore’s official player page documents Jackson’s ankle injury and his recent progression back to limited practice. That provides context for his participation, but it does not settle his availability against Cincinnati. Lamar Jackson’s questionable status leaves Baltimore balancing two plans Jackson’s Wednesday, Thursday and Friday designations followed an identical pattern: limited participation. There was no listed setback, but there was also no upgrade to full participation before the final injury report. Rashod Bateman progressed from limited participation Wednesday to full sessions Thursday and Friday while managing a shoulder injury. Matthew Hibner followed that same progression with a hand issue. Baltimore also received encouraging participation from several offensive linemen. Guards Olaivavega Ioane, John Simpson and Andrew Vorhees each moved from limited work Wednesday to full participation over the final two practices. None received a game designation. Ronnie Stanley’s week requires a more careful reading. Listed with rest, toe and ankle concerns, he went from limited Wednesday to full Thursday before missing Friday. However, he has no game designation. Baltimore has already ruled out safety Jaylinn Hawkins and outside linebacker Tavius Robinson. Tampa is doubtful after three limited practices with a knee issue. Defensive lineman Broderick Washington is questionable following the same participation pattern because of an ankle injury. home.headline: Ravens’ Lamar Jackson practices again, raising hopes for return vs. Bengals
home.blurb: Both Jackson and backup quarterback Tyler Huntley met with the media on Friday afternoon at the Ravens’ Owings Mills practice facility. By rule, teams must make their starting quarterback available to reporters at least once during the week leading up to a game. Having both quarterbacks available, though, was highly unusual. Typically, Jackson meets with reporters every Wednesday during the season. But with his status in question because of an injury, Baltimore waited until Friday each of the past two weeks to rule him out and make Huntley available. Jackson was officially listed as questionable Friday, leaving open the possibility that he could return for Sunday’s pivotal AFC North showdown against the Cincinnati Bengals. He took the podium in shorts and a T-shirt, his left ankle still heavily taped, offering little certainty about what the next two days might bring. Jackson practiced for a third consecutive day Friday, again on a limited basis. On its own, that was encouraging. But practice participation and playing a full game are two different things, and Jackson made it clear that foot pain remains a significant obstacle. The Ravens are also clearly trying to give the Bengals something to think about. There’s also his $260 million contract, which runs through the 2027 season but carries a salary-cap hit of more than $84 million next year. The sides couldn’t hammer out a deal this offseason , so they must address it soon. “If I can just go out there and feel the pain a little bit, I can play,” he said. “But [if] I’m restricted and I can’t do what I do, I’m not helping nobody. If I can just go out there and just be a statue and be hit, that’s not helping my team at all. That’s just me. I feel like I’m being selfish, because it’s about me at that point, for me to go out there and be hurt.” Ravens sack leader Tavius Robinson ruled out for season with injury Ravens outside linebacker Tavius Robinson was ruled out for Sunday after suffering a season-ending pectoral injury . Safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) is also out for this week. Defensive tackle Broderick Washington (tackle) is questionable, while cornerback T.J. Tampa (knee) is doubtful as he continues his return from injured reserve. Will Lamar Jackson play? Or won’t he? “I’m heading in the right direction,” Jackson said in his first comments to reporters since suffering the injury midway through an Oct. 4 win over the Tennessee Titans. “I can’t call it right now. “I feel like the swelling went down a lot, but just the pain tolerance. I’m just trying to move how I move. If I can’t do that, I can’t help my team. I can’t put my team in a situation like that. I feel like I’m doing a disservice then. … I can walk. It’s just trying to run, and [I can’t] put too much pressure.” “Between Lamar and our staff and us, it’s gonna be a decision based on him and how he feels and how effective he can be,” coach Jesse Minter said. “He’s had a good couple days, but we’ll see how it goes over the next 48 hours.

Can the Giants win? Of course. Will they? It's hard to predict. But here are four bold predictions for the Giants-Texans game Sunday. Cam Skattebo Will Score a Touchdown Skattebo hasn't found pay dirt since Week 1 against the Dallas Cowboys. But after his zero-touch performance in the Giants' 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints, Skattebo is poised to bounce back with J.J. McCarthy at quarterback and plodding veteran Najee Harris out of the picture. Skattebo scored in Jaxson Dart's only full game this season, and McCarthy boasts a Dart-style skill set. That should open up Skattebo to a bigger game. J.J. McCarthy Will Throw 2 Touchdowns and at Least 1 Interception The Giants need to stay balanced with Skattebo and reserve running back Tyrone Tracy Jr., but their best offensive matchup is McCarthy, Isaiah Likely and Malik Nabers against the 27th-ranked Texans passing defense. So even though offensive coordinator Matt Nagy wants to have a run-first offense, McCarthy may end up pitching the ball around, especially in the second half. McCarthy has more interceptions (13) than touchdowns (12) in his NFL career, so he'll likely turn it over at least once. Isaiah Likely and Malik Nabers Will Stay Hot The Giants passing offense broke out with Jameis Winston at quarterback, and McCarthy should be able to keep the momentum going against one of the league's worst pass defenses. McCarthy targeted Likely and Nabers quite a bit after he took over for Winston in the fourth quarter, since those two are matchup nightmares for the Texans. Houston also won't have safeties Jalen Pitre and Reed Blankenship, which means the deep middle of the field will be open. But McCarthy may also target rookie Malachi Fields, since both of Fields' receptions came with the 23-year-old quarterback last week. The Giants Will Be in the Game in the Fourth Quarter If you're betting, consider Giants +9.5, since they have been resilient and defying expectations all season. McCarthy nearly led them back from a 24-point fourth-quarter deficit against New Orleans. away.headline: New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything
away.blurb: This will also make New York a step slower in its front seven, which will not only affect the pass rush (Edmunds actually has a couple of sacks this season), but also its pass coverage, which was already questionable. New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Brewers' stunning comeback New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything (Sam Navarro-Imagn Images) Matthew Schmidt Sat, October 24, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads As if the New York Giants didn't already have enough injuries, they just lost yet another key players for the year, as linebacker Tremaine Edmunds has gone down with a season-ending shoulder injury. Edmunds popped up on the injury report this week with the shoulder issue, but it didn't appear to be too big of a deal. Evidently, it was more serious than initially anticipated. Now, the Giants have lost the anchor of their linebacking corps, the man they signed to a three-year, $36 million contract in free agency back in March. New York's run defense was already struggling as it was, so to subtract Edmunds on top of that will make things that much more challenging for Big Blue. Micah McFadden will now step back into a starting role, and fortunately, he has long proven to be serviceable — but he is a definitive downgrade from Edmunds. This injury changes absolutely everything for the Giants. Edmunds' absence will now put that much more pressure on rookie Arvell Reese, and it also means that Reese's mentor will no longer be on the field with him. Reese has looked spectacular in certain moments this year, but he has also looked very much like a first-year player at other times, so losing Edmunds will unquestionably have an effect on the youngster. And of course, it will also give running backs yet even more of a chance to break through the Giants' linebacking corps and into the defensive backfield. New York has now lost two of its top defensive players in Edmunds and Brian Burns, which is beyond devastating for a unit that displayed so much potential during the season opener. The Giants are now incredibly thin on that side of the ball, and in an NFC East that is totally up for grabs, New York may slowly be losing its advantage. To make matters worse, the schedule is about to get tougher. The Giants will face the suddenly hot Houston Texans on the road on Sunday before heading into their bye week. Then, New York will begin a difficult stretch that runs all the way through Week 18. Even in such a horrendous division, it's becoming harder and harder to view the Giants as a potential playoff team given all of their injuries. First, Jaxson Dart . Then Burns. Now Edmunds. It continues to snowball.

But in any event, he is forced to miss time; keep an eye on Foster Moreau, fresh off of his two-touchdown day. Tank Dell is officially set to make his return to the NFL field this weekend. He's now logged multiple full practices over the past three weeks and will be designated for return from injured reserve for his first game in over 650 days. Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans spoke about Dell's pending return earlier this weekend: "I expect Tank just to be himself, and just play the offense the right way," Ryans said. "No huge expectations for what he needs to do. We're all just going to be excited... I'm just thankful, grateful for him to have this opportunity to return." "I don't have any expectations, I'm just happy to see him out there. And that's the only thing that matters." In the Chicago Bears 30-24 win over the New England Patriots , they triumphed despite allowing one of the most unique "Hail Mary" touchdown passes in recent memory. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's 48-yard checkdown touchdown pass to running back Rhamondre Stevenson was the only touchdown pass in the last 20 years in the final 10 seconds of a half, 40-plus yards from the end zone on a throw of 10 or fewer air yards, per CBS Sports Research. What other craziness could happen during the rest of the NFL's Week 7 lineup? Daniel Jones cuts through Brian Flores' No. 1 Vikings defense The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0, and it is very much on the strength of defensive coordinator Brian Flores' aggressive unit. They are an immovable object. Flores' defense leads the NFL in: Scoring defense (12.8 points per game allowed) Third down defense (22.2% third down conversion rate allowed) Red zone defense (27.3% red zone touchdown rate allowed) Goal-to-go defense (33.3% goal-to-go touchdown rate allowed) Completion percentage allowed (53.2%) Touchdown-to-interception ratio allowed (3-6) Sack rate (9.8%) Pressure rate (46.4%) Blitz rate (69.8%) The Vikings' blitz rate of just under 70% (69.8%) is the highest by any team in any five-game span in the last 10 seasons, per CBS Sports Research. So how is that going to go for Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones in Week 7? Well, the bold prediction here is that he doesn't commit any turnovers and totals multiple touchdowns against Flores' unit. Jones' splits versus the blitz are the exact same in terms of yards per pass attempt this season (5.9), and he actually has a higher completion percentage, touchdown-to-interception ratio, and passer rating against the blitz in 2026. Jones also got to spend the second half of the 2024 season watching how Flores' unit operates up close in practice on a daily basis after Minnesota scooped him up for depth purposes after his New York Giants release. That practice experience against Flores will allow Jones to produce a clean, efficient performance. Daniel Jones vs. the blitz, 2026 season Pass attempts Completion percentage Pass yards per attempt Air yards per attempt Passer rating Bijan Robinson goes runs wild vs. the undefeated 49ers The undefeated San Francisco 49ers not only have a top-five scoring offense (29.5 points per game) but also a top-10 scoring defense (18.3 points allowed per game). That also extends to their run defense, which ranks as the seventh-best in football, allowing just 90.2 rushing yards per game. Bijan Robinson , who enters Week 7 leading the NFL with 785 yards from scrimmage, will go off for 150-plus rushing yards against San Francisco. He'll be well rested after having just 11 touches in Week 6, his fewest in a game since 2024, and Robinson will break what has been one of the 49ers' biggest strengths: their control of outside-zone runs. San Francisco has curbed outside-zone runs to just 3.2 yards per carry, the sixth-fewest in the NFL, and they are the only defense that hasn't allowed a gain of 10 or more yards on those runs, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. They have also tackled rushers for a loss or no gain on 5 of 29 outside-zone carries, 17.2%. Robinson has 10 explosive runs (gains of 10 or more yards) on his 65 outside-zone carries, tied with Derrick Henry for the most in the league. He's also only been stuffed for no gain or a loss on 6 of his 65 outside-zone run carries. Robinson will repeatedly cook the 49ers, rushing to the outside, and he'll become not only the first player with over 100 yards rushing against San Francisco in 2026 but the first player to hit at least 150 yards rushing against San Francisco. Cardinals stun Broncos without scoring a touchdown The Arizona Cardinals (2-4) upset the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams 18-16 in Week 6 as 13.5-point road underdogs, earning the second-largest upset win by any team in the last five seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. They accomplished that feat despite not finding the end zone one time. Arizona's 18 points came from six made field goals. The Cardinals host the Denver Broncos (4-2) while seeking their first win away from SoFi Stadium -- both of Arizona's wins have come on the road against the Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers . Denver enters Week 7 with a top 10 scoring defense (20.8 points per game, 10th in the NFL), but Arizona will upset them too for their first home win of the season. Even more impressively, the Cardinals will also beat the Broncos without scoring a touchdown, just like they did with the Rams in Week 6. How will that work? Arizona will pull off that near-impossibility thanks to the Broncos' offensive ceiling being capped by starting quarterback Bo Nix . Nix's 5.6 yards per pass attempt are the fewest in the NFL among quarterbacks to start every game in 2026, and his 4.9 air yards per pass attempt represent the shortest average pass length through six games in the last 20 seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. Not having to defend the deep ball will allow the Cardinals to get creatively aggressive on defense, and Nix will give Arizona's similarly shaky offense, led by journeyman Jacoby Brissett, enough latitude to win with six or seven made field goals and no touchdowns. J.J. McCarthy avoids being sacked vs. Will Anderson Jr., Texans The New York Giants have a new starting quarterback for Week 7 at the Houston Texans : Minnesota Vikings' 2024 10th overall pick castoff J.J. McCarthy . He ranked dead last in the NFL in completion percentage (57.6%), touchdown-to-interception ratio (11-12) and passer rating (72.6) among 33 qualified quarterbacks in 2025. He also had a 10% sack rate last season, the third highest in the entire league. However, McCarthy will not be sacked in his debut as the Giants' starting quarterback despite facing the Houston Texans and All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. , the NFL's sacks leader with 7.5 entering Week 7. How will that happen? Perhaps McCarthy has taken a big leap from 2025 to 2026. After checking in for a benched Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter in Week 6, McCarthy threw for 243 yards, the most by any quarterback in the play-by-play era (since 1991) who had no passing yards in the first three quarters, per CBS Sports Research. The humbling he took, being traded for a 2027 fifth-round pick, plus playing in a more simplistic offense in New York under offensive coordinator Matt Nagy and senior offensive assistant Greg Roman, will allow McCarthy to play a cleaner game in Week 7. That will help him avoid Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter's clutches as he avoids being sacked all game long. Dolphins take a lead for the first time this season The Miami Dolphins ' 2026 season is going exactly as one would expect for a franchise paying more for players not on its roster (an NFL-record $179 million in dead cap hits) than for the players on its roster ($156 million). They're 0-5 and have the NFL's worst scoring offense, averaging 14 points per game. They're also just the second team in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to not have a lead in the first five games of a season, along with the 2005 Houston Texans, per CBS Sports Research. However, they will acquire their first lead in a game of the 2026 season against the New York Jets . The Jets have the worst red zone offense (37.5%) in the NFL, and they haven't scored a touchdown on their last seven red zone trips, which spans the last three games. New York has also been outscored 100-6 in the final two minutes of the first half under Aaron Glenn. Miami will capitalize on Glenn's end-of-the-first-half mismanagement and take a lead in a game for the first time this season. Nix has been a shell of himself through six weeks in the 2026 season, yet Denver is somehow 4-2 and favored on the road against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. Arizona is coming off a massive upset win on the road against the Los Angeles Rams, and while it may not be a playoff team, the Cardinals are not a pushover this season. Jacoby Brissett and Co. will have their work cut out for them against a Denver defense that is one of the best in the NFL. The Bronco offense (29th in success rate) hasn’t been able to get much going during this 4-2 start, but the defense has forced 10 turnovers and is allowing just 5.0 yards per play. The play on that side of the ball has stayed intact even with Pat Surtain II (missed the last two games) and Talanoa Hufanga (missed Week 6) injured. Arizona’s defense is one of the weaker ones that the Broncos have on the schedule, so Sean Payton may look to get his young quarterback going early on Sunday. Will it lead to a Denver win? All season long, the SI Betting team is sharing final score predictions for every NFL game, and we’re hoping it’ll help our readers decide on some spread, moneyline and total bets along the way. Plus, who doesn’t want to get an exact score bet right during the season? Denver is favored on the road, but can bettors trust this offense with Nix struggling? This spread suggests we could see a close game, so let’s dive right into my score prediction for this Week 7 battle. Broncos vs. Cardinals Score Prediction This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan continued his quest to bet on every NFL game in his Road to 272 column . In this matchup, he’s taking Denver to win and cover despite some early struggles on offense: You can throw all of the Broncos' middling metrics out the window, because no team has had a tougher schedule to begin the season than Denver. They've faced the Chiefs, Jaguars, Rams, 49ers, Chargers, and Seahawks, and came out on the other end of that run with a 4-2 record. Despite playing that good a record, their defense still ranks sixth in opponent EPA per play and fifth in opponent success rate. Just imagine how good this defense is going to look when facing lower-tier competition. The Cardinals may be coming off the upset of the year over the Los Angeles Rams, but they enter this week ranking dead last in the NFL in net yards per play at -1.4. Their offense is solid at times, but their defense remains one of the worst units in the league. Give me the Broncos as road favorites. MacMillan has confidence in the Broncos this week, but I’m eyeing the UNDER with the Denver offense looking like one of the worst in the NFL. Arizona’s offense has been able to move the ball with Brissett under center, but Denver has been an elite defense the last few weeks, moving up into the top-12 in the league in points allowed, yards per play allowed, EPA/Play and success rate. The Cardinals are ninth in success rate and 15th in EPA/Play on offense, yet they’ve still scored 21 or fewer points in three of their six games. I expect Brissett to have a much tougher time against a Denver pass defense that – without Pat Surtain II – dominated Seattle and Los Angeles in back-to-back weeks. On the other side of the ball, how can anyone bet on Denver to put up points? The UNDER has hit in five of the Broncos’ six games this season, partially due to the fact that they’ve scored 23 or fewer points in five games and 20 or fewer points in four games. A week ago, the discussion surrounding this team centered on the job security of general manager Monti Ossenfort, defensive coordinator Nick Rallis and quarterback Jacoby Brissett. The season appeared to be spiraling toward a similar finish to last year's 3-14 record. Now, it suddenly feels as if Mike LaFleur has his operation on the right track in Year 1 as head coach. The vibes are good again. Week 7 offers a unique test of those vibes. The Denver Broncos come to town, armed with an elite defense and a miserable offense. The Cardinals offense, in turn, will aim to show that it can hang with the best. The Cardinals defense will aim to avoid a deflating comedown after last week's performance. (Kiyoshi Mio/Imagn Images) 1 / 20 Arizona Cardinals visit NFC West foe Los Angeles Rams in Week 6 Arizona Cardinals visit NFC West foe Los Angeles Rams in Week 6 It's a fascinating matchup. Denver Broncos (4-2) at Arizona Cardinals (2-4) Time/site: 1:05 p.m. MST, State Farm Stadium, Glendale, Arizona. TV: CBS . Radio: 98.7. Last time they played: It's been four years since the Cardinals faced the Broncos. They lost 24-15 in one of the final games of the Kliff Kingsbury era. These rosters have more familiarity, though, from a joint practice in August 2025, in which the Broncos had the clear upper hand on both sides of the ball. Series history: The Cardinals are 1-10-1 all-time against Denver, their worst record against any opponent. The lone win came in 2010, when John Skelton beat Kyle Orton late in what was a lost season for both teams. Coaching matchup On offense, LaFleur will have to find solutions for Vance Joseph, the former Cardinals defensive coordinator who has seen his star rise since joining Denver in 2023. On the other side of the ball, Broncos head coach Sean Payton recently took playcalling duties back from offensive coordinator Davis Webb, who was seen as one of the league's ascendant young coaches entering the season. Rallis will aim to exploit the disarray. Arizona will win if… Its defense pressures Bo Nix: Nix has been bad in general this season, but he's been especially poor against pressure, with eight turnover-worthy plays on 80 dropbacks. That's one of the worst rates in the league, so the Cardinals will aim to make him uncomfortable, as they did with Matthew Stafford last week. Its run game improves: The Cardinals don't need to score 30 points to win this game, but they do need to find some offensive answers. Even without Jeremiyah Love , that likely starts with getting a sputtering rushing attack going. Denver's otherwise vaunted defense ranks 25th in yards per carry allowed. LaFleur finds a way to unlock Michael Wilson: In two games since Marvin Harrison Jr. was traded, Wilson has just eight catches for 62 yards on 14 targets. Compare that to last season, when Wilson averaged 97.2 yards per game when Harrison was out. It won't be easy against Pat Surtain, but to find an explosive element, this offense needs to get Wilson more involved. Denver will win if… The turnover machine keeps rolling: The Broncos defense has sacrificed some down-to-down efficiency this season to become a turnover machine. After ranking 27th in takeaways last year, they rank third this year, with 10 in six games. As underdogs, the Cardinals can't afford to give the ball away in this one. It leans into man coverage: The Cardinals have struggled mightily against man coverage this season but, for some reason, the Rams shied away from those looks last week. It seems like an easy button to press for a Broncos secondary that has the talent to take away Trey McBride and Michael Wilson one-on-one. Its defense stops the Cardinals' three-tight end sets: The Cardinals offense has one clear matchup advantage in this game. They use 13 personnel (one RB, three TEs) at the highest rate in the league. The Broncos defense, meanwhile, has been a bottom-three unit against those looks. That mismatch could enable the Cardinals offense to find more success than expected in this game. Mike LaFleur on Vance Joseph's Broncos defense: "They're very smart, they're very well coached. I have as much respect for VJ as anyone in this league. They do it their own way. … It's got an old-school approach to it in terms of some of their coverages. And that's a credit to them." Sean Payton on the Cardinals defense, after their performance against the Rams: "This is a pressure defense. They give you some looks where they were problematic for the Rams. They were able to take a really good offense and a good quarterback and put them out of rhythm. So we're going to have to have the right answers." By the numbers 1 — Denver's strength of schedule ranking so far this season. The Cardinals rank third. Both these teams may be better than their records indicate. 3.2 — The Cardinals' points per drive when they get at least one first down. That ranks 10th in the league. But they go three-and-out at a top-five rate in the league, holding their offense back. 6.0 — Nix's average depth of target, the lowest in the league. Yet, his time to throw is the sixth-longest in the league. He is neither getting the ball in his playmakers' hands quickly nor pushing the ball downfield. It's a bad combination. 18.7 — Points per game allowed by the Broncos since the start of the 2024 season. No defense has been better over that span. 36.1% — The Cardinals' blitz rate in Week 6. In the first five weeks, that number was 25.6%, a bottom-10 rate in the league. Who will win and why Broncos 24, Cardinals 20: The Cardinals offense matches up surprisingly well with this vaunted Broncos defense, while Denver's own offensive struggles could open the door to another Arizona upset. Still, the Broncos' talent advantage gives them a slight edge. This article originally appeared on Arizona Republic: Cardinals vs Broncos prediction. Can Arizona pull off another upset?

away.headline: Cardinals get troubling Jeremiyah Love injury update before Broncos game
away.blurb: Arizona held Love out of last week’s matchup against the Los Angeles Rams, giving the rookie additional time to recover from his ankle injury. For Love, the priority remains getting healthy enough to return without risking another setback. While Arizona has not officially ruled him out for Sunday, the latest report suggests the team may need to prepare for another game without one of its most important young offensive players. Giants DC Threatens Players Amid 'Unacceptable' Behavior, Calls Out 'Traitors' The Arizona Cardinals could be without one of their most promising offensive weapons for another week. Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love is expected to miss Sunday’s matchup against the Denver Broncos as he continues recovering from an ankle injury, according to CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz. Love already missed Arizona ‘s Week 6 victory over the Los Angeles Rams, and the latest report suggests the Cardinals could be forced to play without their starting running back for a second consecutive game. The former Notre Dame standout did not participate in Wednesday’s practice, raising further concerns about his availability heading into Week 7. Love has been dealing with an ankle injury that initially surfaced following Arizona’s Week 4 matchup against the New York Giants. Although he returned to action against the Detroit Lions in Week 5, the rookie struggled to find his rhythm, finishing with just 22 rushing yards on 12 carries. Before being sidelined, Love had rushed for 245 yards and one touchdown on 67 carries through five games. He also contributed 11 receptions for 36 yards and another touchdown. Arizona selected Love with the third overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, making him the highest-drafted running back since Saquon Barkley went second overall in 2018. The Cardinals entered the season with high expectations for the former Fighting Irish star, who established himself as one of college football’s most explosive offensive players. Now, his early NFL career has been interrupted by injuries. away.blurb: Given the gauntlet of opponents the Broncos faced to get to 4-2, they earned those three days. The question is whether that chance to breathe gave Sean Payton enough time to tweak the Broncos' offense, dig Bo Nix out of his slump, and get the run game firing on all cylinders. The Broncos are starting to get healthier. That may be a relative term, given that three players have been ruled out, but it's more about the caliber of players returning. Surtain is questionable after returning to practice on Wednesday . He was limited all three days this week, so if he's fully healthy, he'll play. If not, the Broncos will be wise and wait until Week 8 to insert him back into the lineup. Coleman is also listed as questionable, but only because Sean Payton wants Arizona to wonder for as long as possible whether the Broncos will actually activate their rookie running back. The Broncos started Coleman's clock to return from injured reserve earlier this week. It's great to see Moss back to full participation. And Waddle has been fully cleared, though he was limited the first two days of the week. Badie, Elliss, and Hufanga are out this week. It wouldn't be a surprise to see Badie and Elliss placed on IR to make room for Coleman and the return of veteran rush linebacker Jonathon Cooper, who's expected to come back from the commissioner's exempt list this week. home.blurb: Arizona held Love out of last week’s matchup against the Los Angeles Rams, giving the rookie additional time to recover from his ankle injury. For Love, the priority remains getting healthy enough to return without risking another setback. While Arizona has not officially ruled him out for Sunday, the latest report suggests the team may need to prepare for another game without one of its most important young offensive players. Giants DC Threatens Players Amid 'Unacceptable' Behavior, Calls Out 'Traitors' The Arizona Cardinals could be without one of their most promising offensive weapons for another week. Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love is expected to miss Sunday’s matchup against the Denver Broncos as he continues recovering from an ankle injury, according to CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz. Love already missed Arizona ‘s Week 6 victory over the Los Angeles Rams, and the latest report suggests the Cardinals could be forced to play without their starting running back for a second consecutive game. The former Notre Dame standout did not participate in Wednesday’s practice, raising further concerns about his availability heading into Week 7. Love has been dealing with an ankle injury that initially surfaced following Arizona’s Week 4 matchup against the New York Giants. Although he returned to action against the Detroit Lions in Week 5, the rookie struggled to find his rhythm, finishing with just 22 rushing yards on 12 carries. Before being sidelined, Love had rushed for 245 yards and one touchdown on 67 carries through five games. He also contributed 11 receptions for 36 yards and another touchdown. Arizona selected Love with the third overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, making him the highest-drafted running back since Saquon Barkley went second overall in 2018. The Cardinals entered the season with high expectations for the former Fighting Irish star, who established himself as one of college football’s most explosive offensive players. Now, his early NFL career has been interrupted by injuries. With Love expected to remain sidelined, Arizona could once again turn to Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight to handle the rushing responsibilities. The Cardinals leaned on their running back depth during last week’s victory, but facing Denver presents another challenge for an offense attempting to establish consistency. The Cardinals have invested heavily in the rookie’s long-term future, and his availability will be an important storyline as the season progresses. picks.blurb: Odds Detroit Lions Beat Green Bay Packers in Week 7 Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI On Sunday afternoon, the Detroit Lions will take on a red-hot Green Bay Packers team that has won three straight games. Most recently, the Matt LaFleur-led squad dispatched of the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football, 23-13. It marked the third consecutive game in which Green Bay held its opponent to 14 or fewer points. And on the season, the Packers’ defense – coordinated by former Arizona Cardinals head coach Jonathan Gannon – has allowed the 10th-fewest points in the NFL (20.8/game). Meanwhile, on the opposite side of the ball, Green Bay – led under center by sixth-year passer Jordan Love – has scored the 10th-fewest points in the game (21.2/game). Through six weeks, Love has also completed just 59.7 percent of his pass attempts. If the season ended today, it'd rank as his lowest completion percentage as a starting quarterback in the NFL. Yet, multiple Green Bay pass-catchers have flourished, most notably wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Watson, now in his fifth NFL season, has already amassed as many touchdowns as last season (six) and nearly as many receptions (29) and reception yards as he did a year ago (538). The former second-round pick secured 35 catches and 611 yards in 10 games a season ago. Meanwhile, Golden, Green Bay's first-round pick in 2025, has already surpassed all his receiving totals from his rookie campaign. He's already racked up 30 catches, 501 yards and three touchdowns amid a career breakout season. And just like Watson, he's well on pace for a 1,000-yard receiving campaign. Consequently, both Watson and Golden possess the potential to wreak havoc against the Lions’ secondary, even with Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch back in the fold for Detroit. In addition to Watson and Golden, the Lions will also likely have their hands full with Packers running back Josh Jacobs. The Pro Bowler returns to the lineup after spending the first six weeks of the season on the commissioner exempt list for an offseason domestic abuse incident. Jacobs, who's coming off a 929-yard, 13-touchdown rushing campaign in 2025, should provide an immediate boost to Green Bay's league-worst ground game. In case you were wondering, the Packers have compiled a measly 359 total rushing yards through the season's first six games. Expect Jacobs, along with Watson and Golden, to give Kelvin Sheppard's defense its fair share of fits on Sunday. However, at this present juncture, I'm still willing to give the Lions a 60 percent chance to pull off the Week 7 victory at home. After a 1-2 start to the season, the Pack have won three games in a row, dominating the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday night in Week 6. Green Bay’s offense has been one of the more explosive passing games in the league, which is a concern for a short-handed Lions secondary that is dead last in the league in EPA/Play this season. Plus, Josh Jacobs is in line to make his 2026 debut for the Packers, the first time they’ll be close to full strength on the offensive side of the ball. Detroit (3-2) is looking to come out of the bye with a home win, and it’s been an elite offense with Jahmyr Gibbs and Goff leading the way. All four NFC North teams could make the playoffs this season, so head-to-head tiebreakers may loom large later on in 2026. All season long, the SI Betting team is sharing final score predictions for every NFL game, a fun way to help bettors decide on spread, total and moneyline bets. This NFC North matchup is the highlight of the late slate on Sunday, as both teams are looking to get a leg up with everyone in this division over .500 through the first six-plus weeks of the season. Packers vs. Lions Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Packers +3 (-110) Lions -3 (-110) Packers: +140 53.5 (Over -110/Under -110) The Lions remain three-point favorites on Sunday – the same price they opened at – but the total has moved up from 52.5 to 53.5 after another strong Green Bay showing in Week 6. The Lions’ defense has been one of the worst in the league this season, and oddsmakers seem to think a shootout is very possible. Packers vs. Lions Score Prediction This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan continued his quest to bet on every NFL game in his Road to 272 column . In this matchup, he’s taking Detroit to come out of the bye with a win: We all know how bad the Lions' defense has been this season, but they're getting some reinforcement coming off their bye week. Their star safety, Brian Branch, is set to make his first start of the season since suffering an injury last year. While he may not be able to completely turn this defense around himself, his boost to their secondary can't be understated. All he has to do is help the Lions' defense force even just a few more punts, and if he can do that, Detroit is going to be in great shape. Their offense is one of the best in the league, ranking sixth in EPA per play and fifth in success rate. Green Bay has been a much better defensive team than the Lions this season, and the return of Josh Jacobs should help boost a running game that has been one of the worst in the league. While MacMillan is on the Lions to cover, I think this could be a high-scoring affair with the Packers’ big-play ability in the passing game. The Lions are dead last in the league in EPA/Play on defense and third on offense, hitting the OVER in all five of their games to date. Last week, the team's matchup with the Dallas Cowboys at Lambeau Field stayed well under the total, thanks in large part to an excellent effort by Jonathan Gannon's defense. This week, however, could be a very different story. On Sunday afternoon, the Packers play the Detroit Lions at Ford Field, a venue that has been the site of several high-scoring games between these two teams in recent years. FanDuel Sportsbook has the total points line set at 52.5 once again, the highest line for a game between these two teams since 2020, when it was set at a whopping 55.5. But since 2020, these two teams have generally scored early and often on the fast turf in Detroit: 2020: Packers win 31-24 (total: 55) 2021: Lions win 37-30 (total: 67) 2022: Lions win 15-9 (total: 24) 2023: Packers win 29-22 (total: 51) 2024: Lions win 34-31 (total: 65) 2025: Packers win 31-24 (total: 55) That's five of the last six games between these two teams in this venue going over 50 points, with four of them hitting 55 or more and two of them reaching a whopping 65 points. It's just what these teams do — well, except for in 2022, a game that was a bizarre defensive slugfest. But look at those results starting in 2023, when Jordan Love took over at quarterback — the Packers haven't scored fewer than 29 points at Ford Field with him behind center. Who will win the game? That's less certain, as the results above show, with the two teams each taking three of the last six games at Ford Field. APC is a bit split on this one, as you'll see in our picks below. But one thing we're not split on is taking the over. Given the Packers' issues defending against an elite running back earlier this year — and considering Jahmyr Gibbs is certainly in the Bijan Robinson echelon — plus the Lions' abysmal passing defense, this game should shape up to be a wild one.
