away.headline: Green Bay Packers RB Josh Jacobs contrite as he prepares to play again amid ongoing NFL investigation
away.blurb: The NFL is still investigating Jacobs over the incident, so the league still could hand out more discipline to the three-time Pro Bowl running back. But for now, Jacobs is eligible to play again for the Packers after missing the first six games of the season. “I thought I’d be playing sooner,” Jacobs said. “But, you know, the optics of everything, I understand the other side. For me, like I said, I’m just grateful to be able to play. It was one of them things where I didn’t want to sit the whole year and then figure it out. I’m just grateful to be back on the team and to be back playing.” Today's E-Editions Chicago Tribune Advertise with Us Advertise with Us Branded Content Paid Partner Content Print (Opens in new window) Print Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email GREEN BAY — Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs expressed contrition as he returned to practice Wednesday and talked with reporters for the first time since pleading no contest to two misdemeanor charges stemming from a May altercation with his then-girlfriend during which she said he threw her to the ground. “Obviously, man, I’m remorseful and sorry for putting this team in this situation,” Jacobs said. “Sometimes when you go through life, situations occur and a four-second, three-second decision can alter your life, honestly.” Jacobs was removed this week from the commissioner’s exempt list, which had prevented him from playing or practicing. The NFL had placed Jacobs on that list Aug. 30 , shortly after charges were filed against him . He pleaded no contest last month to misdemeanor counts of battery and criminal damage to property. The Packers (4-2) face the Lions on Sunday in Detroit. Jacobs was arrested May 26 , three days after police officers came to his Wisconsin home to investigate a disturbance. According to police, the woman told them that Jacobs grabbed her and threw her to the ground as she was trying to exit a garage door, causing her to hit her head. Police said Jacobs also took her phone from her while she was on the ground. Police said they noticed redness on her face and neck and could feel a bump on the back of her head. The criminal complaint against him noted that a surveillance video from the camera system in their garage corroborated the woman’s statement. Both Jacobs and the victim have gone to court attempting to have that video and other evidence sealed permanently . home.blurb: The Packers officially added Love to their injury report with a new back injury ahead of Sunday afternoon's game in Detroit and listed him as an estimated limited participant for their "jog-through" practice session on Wednesday, October 21. Who is Packers' Backup QB if Jordan Love Sits Out? The Packers are still a long few days away from being anywhere close to potentially ruling out Love for Week 7's road game against the Lions. Even so, it is worth examining their fallback plan at quarterback if Love's injury holds him out. The Packers would need to add Slovis to their 53-man roster to have him available as their emergency third quarterback against the Lions. They could also just elevate him and make him active, but that would leave three active quarterbacks — unless they become certain Love won't play. All four players were estimated limited participants for Wednesday's walkthrough. Defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles) was also a limited participant as he continues to work through his 21-day practice window to return from injured reserve. picks.blurb: Raiders vs. Rams Week 7 expert picks and predictions for Sunday's game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers' stunning comeback Valkyries even WNBA Finals Kimi Antonelli on US GP pole NFL injury updates Tatum downplays beef Raiders vs. Rams Week 7 expert picks and predictions for Sunday's game Marvin Uzor, Raiders Wire Sat, October 24, 2026 at 11:50 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Last week, Sports Illustrated's Conor Orr was nearly the sole holdout in picking the Raiders to edge past the Buffalo Bills . Well, anyone backing the Raiders in Week 7 has a lot more company, with a good chunk of the experts giving them a real shot against the Rams Sunday at Allegiant Stadium. Covering the spread against Buffalo apparently buys a team some respect. The computer models still like the Rams comfortably, but some of the humans are far less sure, and a few of them switched sides from last week. Even the Raiders Wire staff is on board too, picking the Raiders 3-1 with an average score of 27-25. NFL.com's panel can barely agree Three of NFL.com's five analysts picked the Rams, with Jeremy Bergman at 24-17, Gennaro Filice at 27-24 and Dan Parr at 31-27. The other two went with the Raiders, and both picks come with a story. Bobby Kownack had the Bills hanging 35 points on the Raiders last week. Now he has the Raiders winning a 17-14 rock fight , which is quite a change of heart in seven days. Brooke Cersosimo has the Raiders by one at 25-24, and the Rams clearly gave her more to think about than she expected. "Of all the teams in the league, I would not have guessed the Rams would give me pause at this point in the season," Cersosimo wrote. She also has the game ending on a Raiders field goal in the final minute. Bleacher Report's experts traded seats The funniest twist came from Bleacher Report. Maurice Moton was the panel's lone Raiders backer last week, and this week he jumped to the Rams, while Gary Davenport, who doubted the Raiders against Buffalo, came over to their side. "Why lay this many points on the road against a Raiders team that just covered the same spread against Buffalo?" Davenport wrote. Moton expects the Rams to adjust without Davante Adams by leaning on their tight ends. The panel finished 4-3 in favor of the Raiders against a 4.5-point spread, with Ian Hanford, Wes O'Donnell and Brent Sobleski joining Davenport. Pete Prisco and Mike Florio keep it tight CBS Sports' Pete Prisco picked the Rams to win by a single point, 28-27, which is a polite way of taking the Raiders against the spread. "They still have Matt Stafford. He can light up a defense, which he will do here," Prisco wrote. "But the Rams will give up some big plays to the Raiders, who hang around." The rest of the CBS panel split 4-3 for the Rams against the spread, with Tyler Sullivan and Jamey Eisenberg standing with Prisco. Meanwhile, Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio has the Rams winning 26-23 and sees a season on the line for Los Angeles. "If the Rams get to five losses with 10 games left, they could be done," Florio wrote. The computers aren't buying it The models are far more confident than we (humans). Dimers gives the Rams a 70.8% chance to win with a 26-20 projection, and the Covers AI model has Los Angeles winning 27-20. Five of the seven human score predictions in this roundup land within three points, though. These experts expect another one-score game, and the Raiders have lost two of their last three games by a field goal. picks.headline: Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7
picks.blurb: Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers' stunning comeback Valkyries even WNBA Finals Kimi Antonelli on US GP pole NFL injury updates Tatum downplays beef Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7 Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Thu, October 22, 2026 at 6:41 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads There is a big time injury for the Los Angeles Rams . And the Raiders have a major concern as well. These teams meet in Week 7, and here are bold predictions for the NFL contest. It's a crucial game for the Rams, who stand at 2-4 and find themselves a staggering four games behind the front-running 49ers in the NFC West. Meanwhile, the Raiders stand at 3-3 in third place in the AFC West. They're unlikely to be a playoff contender, but are trying to build a strong foundation for 2027. Let's take a look at what could happen when these teams battle. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Matthew Stafford will throw for three touchdowns It's hard to gauge what kind of yardage output Stafford will have. Without the injured Davante Adams, the Rams may lean on the ground game a little more. Adams is the team's leading receiver with 480 yards and four touchdowns. Sure, Stafford still has Puka Nacua. And Nacua will get his targets and yardage. But who steps into the No. 2 role? Maybe the Rams will use tight end Tyler Higbee more. Or perhaps Konata Mumpfield or Jordan Whittington will step up and produce. However, despite the receiver situation, the Rams will need to find a way to get the ball into the end zone if the Raiders load up to stop the run in the red zone. So look for Stafford to spread it around and still get his TD passes. Stafford said he understands the situation , according to The Athletic. "I just feel even more responsibility to try to be as good as I can be to help us continue to win," Stafford said. "In some of those guys' instances where they're going to have opportunities to hopefully come back and play for us, make sure that when they come back and play for us, it's meaningful stuff for them." However, some observers think Stafford has finally reached the end of his NFL rope, according to ESPN. "Stafford can't move," Ben Solak wrote. "He was never the most mobile quarterback, but the Rams were willing to use him on boots in the past. In 2024, 16.8% of Stafford's pass attempts were on the run — an above-average number! That fell to 13.9% in 2025 and is down to 9.6% in 2026. Sure, designed rollouts are down — but it isn't just that. "Stafford has zero scrambling passing yards on the season per NFL Next Gen Stats. He has yet to break the pocket and complete a pass on a scramble drill. The last quarterback to log no scramble passing yards through six weeks of a season was 2022 Tom Brady — the final season of a pocket passing titan." But it's not time to write Stafford off. Rams RB Kyren Williams will rush for 90-plus yards The Rams must run the football against the Raiders, a team that struggles to stop the ground game. The Raiders are giving up 134.3 yards per game, which ranks No. 28 in the NFL. Keeping the ball on the ground needs to be a big part of the Rams' game plan. The Rams have thrown 252 passes with 148 rushing attempts. McVay wants those numbers closer together , according to theramswire.com. "Ultimately, what I care about and what we care about is what's the best way is to move the ball and score points," McVay said. "Because of some of the situations that we've been in, those two-minute situations have gotten us a little bit out of balance. No matter how I cut it, it's an excuse. I'd like to be able to have a little bit more balance. And that's reflected by being efficient on early downs and sustaining drives." One thing is for sure, Williams and the Rams haven't lost their belief that this can be a special season. "Man, my confidence is still as high as ever," Williams said. "We know what we've got on our team and in this locker room. We come to practice every single week. That's why we can't lose our focus. We can't lose what matters the most, and that's the work. "It's about having faith. That the work we put in every single week will come to shine." Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty will split carries with Mike Washington Jr. There's no doubt that Jeanty has been a huge disappointment for the Raiders. They picked him No. 6 overall, expecting a franchise-changing player. Instead, Jeanty has a career average of 3.5 yards per carry. And Washington has been turning heads with the coaching staff, according to a post on the Raiders' YouTube page via Athlon Sports. But he needs to be better at pass protection . "He's a rookie, so he had a lot to catch up on," Kubiak said when asked about Washington's role in the passing game. "He's continuing to improve. (And) he's putting the work in. You see the practice come to life in the games. He's not where he wants to be. He's got to keep growing." Jeanty has been a threat in the passing game. Maybe his future is as a third-down back. Washington could supplant him. And the prediction is for that to begin this week. Jeanty has time to bounce back. It's still early in his career. But he simply hasn't been able to show in the NFL what he showed in college. away.headline: Rams-Raiders injury report: Trent McDuffie, Nate Landman miss practice
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: On Wednesday, Trent McDuffie and Nate Landman both missed practice. Landman is in the concussion protocol, while McDuffie is still recovering from a groin injury that caused him to sit out Week 6 against the Cardinals. Defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway was the only non-participant for the Raiders. Five other players were limited, including Brock Bowers and Kolton Miller. After dropping their last two games, the Los Angeles Rams are back to work in advance of their Week 7 matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders . The injury bug bit the Rams hard on Sunday, as Davante Adams, Kobie Turner, Poona Ford and Blake Grupe were all lost to IR, so Los Angeles will be shorthanded against Vegas this week. They won't make any excuses, though. Sean McVay said the Rams are monitoring McDuffie's progress to see if he'll be ready to go against the Raiders. McDuffie and Landman were the only players who did not participate in practice. Josh Wallace has a calf injury but was a full participant, as was Colby Parkinson (shoulder). This article originally appeared on Rams Wire: Rams-Raiders injury report: Trent McDuffie, Nate Landman miss practice

away.headline: NFL Week 7 Injury Report: Raiders' Quay Walker and Rams' Puka Nacua Listed
away.blurb: Las Vegas Raiders linebacker Quay Walker has been downgraded to questionable with a chest injury ahead of Sunday’s game against the Los Angeles Rams. The change raises uncertainty about his availability for the Week 7 matchup at Allegiant Stadium. ESPN’s Raiders reporter Ryan McFadden reported the downgrade on X on Saturday. Walker had been a full participant in Friday’s practice after being limited on Wednesday and Thursday, according to the Raiders’ official injury report. The injury report also lists running back Mike Washington Jr. as questionable for Las Vegas with foot and back issues. For Los Angeles, wide receiver Puka Nacua is questionable with a calf injury, while linebacker Nate Landman has been ruled out with a concussion. Walker was limited during the first two practices of the week before completing Friday’s session without a game-status designation on the team’s published report. The subsequent downgrade means his availability remains uncertain, although the available reporting does not establish whether he experienced a setback or explain the reason for the change. The Raiders host the Rams on Sunday, Oct. 25, with kickoff scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET. Las Vegas will need to clarify Walker’s status before the game, while his questionable designation leaves open the possibility that he could still play. The late change comes as Las Vegas looks to halt a three-game losing streak. The Raiders enter the matchup at 3-3, third in the AFC West behind the Kansas City Chiefs at 5-0 and Denver Broncos at 4-2. Walker is listed as a linebacker on the Raiders’ roster. His potential absence would give Las Vegas another defensive issue to assess before facing a Rams team that enters Week 7 at 2-4, fourth in the NFC West. Los Angeles has lost its last two games, including a narrow 18-16 defeat to the Arizona Cardinals on Oct. 18.

away.headline: Rams get interesting trade report after Davante Adams' multi-week injury
away.blurb: After such a brutal injury, ESPN's Dan Graziano is reporting that the Rams, even at 2-4, are expected to search the WR trade market for potential additions to try and keep their season alive while Adams is out. It wouldn't make sense to give up now, especially since Garrett should come back, and Adams could return later this season as well. Rams get interesting trade report after Davante Adams' multi-week injury | Sporting News Skip to main content SN 140 Watch Watch How to Watch Streaming Services fubo Add Sporting News on Google div))]:my-4" data-testid="advert--mobile_branded_logo" id="Branded_Logo_Mobile"> The 2-4 Los Angeles Rams are one of the most disappointing teams in the NFL this season. Meant to be a top Super Bowl contender, there's a real chance that the Rams aren't even a playoff team when it's all said and done. But their season isn't over yet. However, the team did just get a crushing piece of news following Week 6, as star wide receiver Davante Adams was revealed to have suffered a serious, multi-week hamstring injury. Rams expected to make trade calls for WR help after Davante Adams injury "I do not expect the Rams to go down without a fight, and my understanding is that they will at least explore the possibility of trading for a wide receiver in the wake of Davante Adams' hamstring injury," Graziano reports. This is a noteworthy development for the Rams, as it shows the team is still trying to compete and make the playoffs from their 2-4 record, despite the 6-0 San Francisco 49ers dominating and the NFC Wild Card being a very tight race. But the Rams potentially adding wide receiver help shouldn't come as a huge surprise, as they had already been one of the teams linked to WRs on the trade market, even before the Adams injury. This is an all-in team after their blockbuster trades for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie. Spending a few more draft picks on WR help wouldn't be a surprise whatsoever. They've already mortgaged their future on this 2026 roster. MORE : ESPN analyst believes Browns are a quarterback away from being Super Bowl contenders While the Rams might not land a blockbuster name like Brian Thomas Jr., someone like Jerry Jeudy would be a solid veteran presence in the WR room to help in the meantime while Adams sits on IR with a serious hamstring injury. They're already all-in for 2026; there's no reason why they shouldn't invest a bit more to bolster a roster that can still do some damage if they make the playoffs. Graziano is reporting that WR help is something Les Snead and Sean McVay will consider adding. While the 2-4 Rams might not seem like a buyer, this team is in too deep to not continue striving for a title in 2026. away.headline: Report: Rams WR Puka Nacua's injury not believed to be serious
away.blurb: Nacua sustained the injury during Thursday's practice and did not participate in Friday's session as the Rams (2-4) prepared to face the Raiders (3-3). The Rams already are without fellow wideout Davante Adams, who was placed on injured reserve earlier in the week with a ruptured hamstring. Remaining Los Angeles wide receivers include Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Alex Bachman. Nacua, 25, has 37 catches for 417 yards and one touchdown to go with one rushing score in four games this season. He missed two games with a hip/groin injury. A two-time Pro Bowl selection, Nacua led the NFL with 129 receptions last season and racked up 1,715 receiving yards with 10 touchdowns in 16 games. home.headline: NFL suspends Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson for 1 game for spitting at Las Vegas Raiders
home.blurb: After splitting the 2024 season between the Rams and Baltimore, White re-signed with the Bills and had 16 starts last season. He didn’t rule out another return to Buffalo after completing his one-year contract last season. Today's E-Editions Chicago Tribune Advertise with Us Advertise with Us Branded Content Paid Partner Content Print (Opens in new window) Print Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. — The NFL on Monday suspended Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson for one game without pay for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders players on the field during a game a day earlier. Gardner-Johnson was ejected late in the second quarter for unsportsmanlike conduct following an exchange with a group of Raiders players, including tight end Brock Bowers. In issuing the suspension, the league cited its rule applying to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.” With Buffalo (5-1) entering its bye week, Gardner-Johnson’s suspension will begin on Oct. 26 and run through Nov. 2, a day after the Bills host the Baltimore Ravens. The player has the right to appeal the suspension. Gardner-Johnson apologized to his teammates immediately following Buffalo’s 33-30 win, and has since posted a note on social media apologizing to fans. “I owe my teammates an apology and to be a man about it,” Gardner-Johnson said following the game. “You got to understand that as a grown man you can’t be doing (stuff) like that in a game,” he added. “As a vet, I’ll be better. I’ll take my consequences as it is, handle it like a man and move on.” The 28-year-old won a Super Bowl with the 2024 Philadelphia Eagles and is on his sixth team in eight seasons. Gardner-Johnson was signed by the Chicago Bears in October 2025 and appeared in 10 games with 51 total tackles. He signed a one-year contract with Buffalo in March. Coach Joe Brady referred to Gardner-Johnson’s spitting act as being “inexcusable,” and said he’s discussed the matter privately with the player. “It can’t happen. That’s not what we’re about. That’s not what the game of football is about, and he knows that,” Brady said. Gardner-Johnson arrived in Buffalo with an established reputation of being a noted trash-talker and as someone who has on occasion crossed the line with illegal hits. “I don’t need a roster of everybody being the same person,” Brady said. “Obviously, he crossed the line yesterday and that can’t happen. It won’t happen again. Personality-wise, I’m not afraid to have people who are going to try to toe the line in everything they do.” Also, the Bills are bringing back a familiar face with cornerback Tre’Davious White agreeing to sign to the team’s practice squad, a person with knowledge of discussions told The Associated Press. This weekend, Seattle will host the 5-0 Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football. Kansas City is coming off a frustrating 2025 campaign, which ended with a record of 6-11. That was the first time they had a losing season under Andy Reid, and they've already turned things around. Much of that is due to Kenneth Walker III, the former Seahawk who has been electric for the Chiefs . Seattle needs to find a way to contain Walker, while also figuring out how to get their ground game on track, which could happen with Zach Charbonnet set to return to action. If they can do that, they will have a chance to score the upset. As the game nears, let's see who the experts believe will walk away with the win this weekend. They will compete in a Sunday Night Football matchup for the second time in 2026 as they head to Seattle to take on the reigning Super Bowl champions. While Andy Reid's squad has yet to drop a game, the Seahawks have struggled to get their offense going in the post-Kenneth Walker era . Amid their two-game losing streak, quarterback Sam Darnold has tossed four interceptions, including one that ultimately gave the Broncos a free victory last week in overtime. Sportsbooks have labeled Seattle as a slight home favorite, but what does the ESPN Matchup Predictor think? Here's what their computer model projects a few days before kickoff. This was undoubtedly circled as one of the more difficult challenges on the Chiefs' schedule heading into the season, and that stands true despite Seattle's early shortcomings. They have the same defensive playmakers who made them a force to be reckoned with in last year's postseason. Even with Darnold's inconsistencies through the air, Jaxon Smith-Njigba remains a premier wide receiver in the league. He leads the NFL in receptions, receiving yards, and receiving touchdowns in spite of the shaky quarterback play. Seattle's passionate 12s will undoubtedly come out in full force, as this game means a lot more to them than it does to the Chiefs. Kansas City obviously wants to preserve its flawless record, but a loss that drops Seattle to 3-4 would likely take the Seahawks out of the division race moving forward. Walker's homecoming to the team he spent his first four years with is a major storyline. He'll be looking to prove why Seattle should have paid him as he continues to establish himself as one of the best running backs in the NFL. The Chiefs have had plenty of breaks go their way and won't stay undefeated forever, but the Seahawks will have a tough time overcoming turnovers from Darnold if they want to win. Unlike some of their past opponents, Patrick Mahomes will make them pay. The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17 San Francisco 49ers (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. It looked like we were in for a blowout after the 49ers went up 23-3, but Washington then outscored San Francisco, 14-0, while outgaining the 49ers 201 yards to 7 yards. This week, I'm going to take the points with Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 22, Falcons 20 Dubin (49ers -3): This line feels several points too low, even with Mike Evans potentially out in addition to all of the other wide receiver issues. And Atlanta can't quite reach the same level offensively — even with Bijan Robinson and Drake London on hand. The two-time NFL MVP was playing some fantastic ball before the unfortunate ankle injury, and it's worth mentioning he's 7-2 in his career against Joe Burrow . I was high on the Bengals entering this season, and I'm not ready to move off that take. I think this Baltimore secondary is in for a tough test in stopping Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The former averages 120.4 receiving yards per game vs. the Ravens, while the latter caught two touchdowns the last time he faced them. Higgins actually hasn't faced Baltimore since Oct. 6, 2024! Before the season started, this looked like a potential swing game for the NFC East standings, but a lot has changed in six weeks. Dallas is off to a slow start at 2-4, and the defense (31st in EPA/Play) remains one of the worst in the NFL. Dak Prescott and Co. have lost back-to-back primetime games against Tampa Bay (Week 5) and Green Bay (Week 6), looking pretty rough in both appearances. So, can they turn things around on the road against a divisional opponent? The Eagles enter this game on a four-game losing streak, and star quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots in his lungs. That is a massive blow to the Eagles in the futures market, as they’re now last in the odds to win the NFC East and +15000 to win the Super Bowl. Tanner McKee is set to make another start in Week 7, and this may turn into a lost season for an Eagles team that could decide to trade some veteran pieces to recoup draft capital and lighten the load on the salary cap in years to come. Oddsmakers have set the Cowboys as favorites in this matchup, and a win would put Dallas in a much better position to win the NFC East – which it is still favored to do. Dallas needs to figure things out on offense, as Prescott has struggled with turnovers (not all his fault) in the last few games while the offensive line allowed him to take a ton of big hits in Week 6. picks.headline: Cowboys vs. Eagles bold predictions for Week 7 Monday Night Football
picks.blurb: Cowboys vs. Eagles bold predictions for Week 7 Monday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers' stunning comeback Valkyries even WNBA Finals Kimi Antonelli on US GP pole NFL injury updates Tatum downplays beef Cowboys vs. Eagles bold predictions for Week 7 Monday Night Football Matty Breisch, ClutchPoints Sat, October 24, 2026 at 11:49 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Sitting at 2-4, the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys are technically tied for second place in the NFC East, but it sure doesn't feel like it. In one corner are the challengers, the Cowboys, who are in the middle of a very Dallas season through Week 6. Their passing game is good, as it often is under Brian Schottenheimer, but their run game is one of the worst in the NFL, recording just 456 yards through six games. On the opposite side of the ball, Christian Parker's defense is also off to a brutal start , ranking 23rd against the pass, 32nd against the run, 30th overall in yards, and 25th in points allowed. Things have gotten so bad that Parker was effectively undermined by Jerry Jones and company, with former Cleveland Browns head coach Mike Pettine hired as a senior defensive assistant in the hopes of getting things back on track. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) And as for the Eagles? Well, it's hard not to know about the drama surrounding Philadelphia at this point, with Jalen Hurts' blood clots among the biggest stories in the NFL so far in October. With injuries piling up, Lane Johnson retired, and Cam Jurgens traded to the Baltimore Ravens, some thought the Eagles might be able to rally around Tanner McKee in Week 6 against the Carolina Panthers, but Sean Mannion's offense remained as frustrating as ever, and Philly fell to 2-4 without too much fight. Now scheduled for their first of two matchups in 2026, a Monday Night Football showdown that likely looked much more appealing on paper when the schedule was initially announced, hopefully the NFC East will at least see a winner for the first time in three weeks, but who will it be? Will the Cowboys finally live up to fan expectations and get a victory, proving they were right to make a number of big trades for star players? Or will the Eagles figure something out now that it's clear Hurts isn't coming back to save the season? Bill Streicher-Imagn Images The Eagles' run game finally gets going regardless of who plays If there's one thing Nick Sirianni teams have always been good at over his tenure, it's running the ball. In 2021, the Eagles had the NFL's top rushing offense, and while Sirianni's squad never reached that mark again, they were top-8 in every year until 2025, when they fell to " only " 18th thanks to a 1,140-yard campaign by Saquon Barkley. In 2026, the Eagles' rushing offense is almost as bad as the Cowboys', but that's almost by design, ranking 29th in rushing yards largely because they've attempted the 28th most rushes of any team in the NFL. For whatever reason, maybe a lack of quarterback runs over the past three weeks, the Eagles have suffered through drives, quarters, and even games where they largely abandon the run, attempting just 18 runs against the Jaguars in Week 5 and 13 in Week 6 against the Panthers. Now granted, the Eagles spent plenty of time playing from behind against the Jaguars and the Panthers and were largely tasked with rolling with backups in both games, with Dameon Pierce the lone running back still on the 53-man roster who played in Week 5, but with McKee locked in Philly's quarterback long-term, establishing the run is paramount to forging an identity down the stretch. Fortunately, the Eagles have the perfect foe to get back on track in the Cowboys, who are as bad at running the ball as they are at defending it. If Barkley can play in Week 6, the Eagles will likely pound the rock with at least a 50-50 run-to-pass ratio in order to make McKee's life easier, but even if he can't, Pierce should flirt with 20 rushes against a team allowing 4.7 yards per carry . If that happens, Parker will be forced to stack his box more and free up downfield shots for players like Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, and Hollywood Brown. Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images. The Cowboys will live or die by the pass Because, again, the Cowboys' rushing attack is as bad as their run defense – and the Eagles have been about average at defending the run in 2026 – if Dallas wants to beat the Birds in Week 7, they will have to do it through the air using their run game. Through Week 6, only one team has attempted more passing attempts than the Cowboys, the Los Angeles Rams, with their 1,603 passing yards ranking sixth, and their 15 passing touchdowns sit at 15th. Because the Cowboys aren't even really trying to establish things on the ground consistently, ranking dead last with 122 attempts on the year, Dallas has had to live or die by the passing game even when they aren't playing from behind while fielding a comeback bid. In Week 7, if the Cowboys wanted to, they could try to get things going on the ground. While the Eagles rank 19th in rushing yards allowed this season, that's coming on the fifth-fewest rushing attempts against in the NFL, with all six of their opponents thus far recording at least 100 yards on the ground. The Eagles are allowing 4.0 rushing yards per attempt, .3 more than the Cowboys are averaging on the year, and if they can just hold those averages, Javonte Williams should be able to make Dak Prescott's life easier. Unfortunately for fans in Dallas, while a consistent offensive game plan could bend Vic Fangio's defense to the point of breaking, when has Schottenheimer shown that conviction? If the Eagles force a few three-and-outs early, when their defense has been their best, the Cowboys might return to their usual ways of trying to beat the Birds with Prescott's arm against a secondary that is very good when everything is firing on all cylinders. Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images The Cowboys "win" on Monday Night Football, if that matters At full strength, the Eagles are a better team than the Cowboys. Yes, Sean Mannion's offense is far from what fans expected, and they've lost a number of key pieces to trade and retirement, but in Weeks 1 and 2, Hurts showed that he's a good enough player to lead even a flawed offense to victory. If Fangio's defense didn't have to play a little over five more minutes per game than the offense , they'd presumably be able to be fresher at the end of games, and that, when coupled with an even average points-per-game average, would be enough to win a woefully disappointing NFC East. Unfortunately, the Eagles are not healthy, and McKee will be under center in Week 7 and beyond, barring another injury, a benching, or a trade for another arm. DeVonta Smith is already out for Monday Night Football , as are Nolan Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, and Michael Carter II, and as the season continues on, it's safe to assume even more injuries will stack up in a seemingly doomed campaign. As a result, the Eagles find themselves at a talent disadvantage, have morale that is shaky at best, and hold no real desire to go all-out to secure the win on Monday Night Football. The Cowboys, by contrast, clearly don't want to be 2-4 and have made win-now trades for players like Joey Porter Jr. to try to fix that ASAP. As a result, if they don't win this game, it will be a massive blemish on their record, which gives Jerry Jones incentive to put the pressure on Schottenheimer to win at all costs. away.blurb: Dallas Goedert is good to go for Monday, while Saquon Barkley and Jalyx Hunt inch closer to a potential return. "It's just kind of the same injury that I sustained earlier. I just had a little bit of inflammation in there, had to let that settle down, but felt really good running out there today," Goedert said after Saturday's practice. "I want to be out there anytime I can. We only get 17 games. To miss a game, to miss two games, it always stinks. So if I can be available, I'm going to do everything I can to play. "I'm going to go out there and do whatever I can to help the team win, whether it's run blocking, pass blocking, or hopefully get a couple catches. We're looking forward to this game playing on Monday night against the division rival. It's going to be a lot of fun. The atmosphere's going to be great and it's a game I wouldn't want to miss." Two of the Eagles' top receivers, DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), have been ruled out, leaving rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon as the primary wide receiver option. "It's definitely a big opportunity with the team," Lemon said. "I'm just super excited to go out there with the guys, put on a good performance. Had a great week of practice with all the guys. So, just trying to go out there and execute. A couple guys are out. So really just, next man up. I got a bunch of trust in the guys next to me, trust in the coaches and the game plan." Running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) took a step forward and was a full participant at practice on Saturday after being limited previously in the week. The running back is listed as questionable for Monday night. Meanwhile, Jonathan Greenard (ankle), who did not practice again on Saturday, is listed as questionable. The edge rusher said it will be a game-time decision as he will need to see how his ankle feels. Alongside Greenard, the outside linebacker room is banged up. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) could return on Monday as he is listed as questionable after practicing in a limited capacity all week. Nolan Smith (concussion) has been officially ruled out. Smith is joined by defensive back Michael Carter II (abdomen). Cornerback Jakorian Bennett, tight end Grant Calcaterra, guard Landon Dickerson, and tight end Eli Stowers all participated fully in practice on Saturday. They are all listed as questionable since they are on Injured Reserve and would need to be activated by Monday afternoon in order to play against the Cowboys.
